page.layout: One printed page, with a text block of running Latin in the centre and a block of italic summary lines below it. The top shows the title and division heading. A facing page's edge with show-through is at the right and is not transcribed. No running head, catchword or signature. The left margin has a small section number "2." beside the first paragraph.

main_text.head: SELECTORUM ANACEPHALÆOSI LIBER PRIMUS.
main_text.p: 2. Iurisprudentię finis est iustitia: iustitię obiectum est ius: quod quadrifariam dividitur. Primo est publicum, aut privatum. 2. Privati autem partes sunt, ius naturale, ius gentium, & ius civile. Secundo, vel est scriptum, vel non scriptum. Tertio, partim est mutabile, partim immutabile. Quarto versatur in personis, aut in rebus, aut in actionibus. 3. Qui ad personas attinet, civium Romanorum alii sunt filiifamilias in potestate parentum constituti, alii patrisfamil.qui sui iuris sunt. 4. Patria potestas constituitur iustis nuptiis, legitima procreatione, 5. & adoptione. 6. Solvitur autem variis modis, 7. alii sunt in tutela, alii in curatione, alii neutrum tenentur. Tutores constituuntur, 8. Aut testamento, 9. lege, ut agnati (10. sed agnatio per capitis deminutionem tollitur,) 11. parentes, 12. & tutores fiduciarii: 13. aut a magistratu. Qui vero tutor datus est, partim negotia pupillar[?] gerit, 14. partim pupillo gerenti auctor fit, 15. donec tutela finiatur: 16. tuncque curatio succedit. 17. Tutoribus autem curatoribus tria communia sunt: satisdatio, 18. excusatio, & ob suspicionem remotio. Hactenus de personis.

page.notes: The page number at the top left is stained and hard to read; "24" is a guess. The word after "pupillar" is cut off by the stain and is marked [?]. The list lines are italic and some words are split at the line ends, and the left edge of the list's final word is faint, so "civili[?]" and "modis[?]" are doubtful. The right edge of the text block runs into the facing page's show-through, which is not transcribed. Some words near the right edge may be partly hidden, and "finiatur" is read from its visible ending. No printing errors were noticed.
